water.name: Land
water.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points (centre + 6) fall on land, and CORINE water covers less than half of it.

water.name: Lake
water.rule: CORINE inland water (water courses and bodies) covers at least half of the hex, or most of its 7 sample points fall in Natural Earth lakes: reservoirs such as Đerdap and Vlasina, and the Danube where it is wider than about 1.5 km.

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 30 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation ≥ 110 m, or mean elevation ≥ 1,400 m.

relief.name: Peaks
relief.rule: Mean elevation ≥ 1,900 m (alpine: Šar, Prokletije, the top of Kopaonik).

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, or no CORINE land pixels.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and broad-leaved (311) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and coniferous (312) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and mixed forest (313), woodland-shrub (324) or agro-forestry (244) the largest type.

cover.name: Scrub
cover.rule: Sclerophyllous vegetation (323) or burnt areas (334) are the largest group.

cover.name: Grassland
cover.rule: Natural grassland (321), heath (322), sparse vegetation (333) and urban green or sports grounds (141, 142) are the largest group.

cover.name: Pasture
cover.rule: Pastures (231) and farmland mixed with natural vegetation (243) are the largest group.

cover.name: Cropland
cover.rule: Arable land, vineyards, orchards and mixed cultivation (211–242) are the largest group.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: Inland marshes and peat bogs (411, 412) are the largest group.

cover.name: Urban
cover.rule: Urban fabric, industry, transport and construction sites (111–124, 133) are ≥ 30% of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

cover.name: Barren
cover.rule: Mines, dumps, sand and bare rock (131, 132, 331, 332) are the largest group: the open-pit mines of Kolubara, Kostolac and Bor show up here.

cover.name: Ice & snow
cover.rule: Glaciers and perpetual snow (335) are the largest group.

notes.water: Serbia has no coast, so every hex is land or lake. Rivers narrower than about 2 km are drawn as lines over land hexes; where the Danube widens (Đerdap, Golubac, below Belgrade) its hexes become water.
notes.relief: From the elevation samples inside each 3 km hex. A hex whose lower 60% of samples is flat lowland is eased one class (valley floors). Water hexes are always flat.
notes.cover: From CORINE Land Cover 2018 (100 m), sampled on a 240 m lattice inside each hex (about 400 points). Water (511, 512) and no-data points are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points, rounded to whole percent, and the urban threshold is applied to the rounded developed share.
